provenance: Authored by hand for teaching. No outcome here is a real result, no compound was tested, and nothing is a safety assessment of any substance. The records are shaped like real ones so the distinctions are legible, and they are not data.
stores: Findings that someone would have had to run an experiment to obtain. Molecular alerts are never stored, because an alert is computed from the structure and storing one beside a measured outcome is the collapse this lab is about.

molecular-alert.obtained_by: matching a substructure pattern against the structure
molecular-alert.what_it_does_not_establish: that anything was measured, that the compound is hazardous, or that the pattern is doing anything in this molecule

assay-outcome.obtained_by: running one assay in one system at one concentration
assay-outcome.what_it_establishes: a readout in that system at that concentration
assay-outcome.what_it_does_not_establish: behaviour in another system, at another concentration, or in an organism

organ-liability.obtained_by: attributing a pattern of findings to an organ, usually across several assays
organ-liability.what_it_does_not_establish: a mechanism, a dose at which it occurs, or that it transfers between species

organism-level.what_it_establishes: what happened to that organism under that exposure
organism-level.what_it_does_not_establish: that the finding generalises to another species or another schedule

alerts.what_they_are: Named substructure patterns. Each is a pattern, and a pattern match is not a finding.

exposure.why_it_matters: Every assay outcome above is a readout at a concentration. Whether it is a risk depends on the exposure a dose actually produces, and no exposure is recorded anywhere in this file. Without it, a positive at 200 micromolar and a positive at 1 micromolar read the same on a profile page and mean entirely different things.
